config.question: Fitted on the arms' own train scores (400 rows/class) instead of held-out rows (40 rows/class), does the integration layer recover the specialist gains that hard routing lost?

registration_notes.N100.1: Registered AFTER M143's sealed negative (fused 0.1463 vs global 0.2251) and its diagnostic (global-only stacking 0.159 vs global 0.2251 on the same fitter = a rows-per-class effect, not a broken fit). This cell does NOT re-adjudicate M143; it re-tests on the train-score axis (epistemic rule 2).
registration_notes.N100.2: Phase 1 scores the full TRAIN split (138k rows) with the six 512-atom specialists (exact M143/M139b construction, bit-exact M119 anchors) and the global head (dual accumulate on the sealed f6144 memmaps); cached to v16/m143b/train_scores.npz (~2.5h GPU).
registration_notes.N100.3: Phase 2 fits the stacking head and the competence router (correct-arm target, lowest-index tie-break) on the train rows; penalty ladder {1,10,100,1000,10000} selected on a seeded 80/20 train-valid slice; evaluated on the sealed TEST scores from v16/m143/scores.npz (never recomputed).
registration_notes.N100.4: Gate (same shape as M143): fired if fused < global - 0.005 on test rows, OR competence < identity, OR identity < random.
registration_notes.N100.5: Smoke runs declare _smoke_note and MUST refuse the sealed output directory.

sparse.specialist_construction: A5-exact (M119/M124/M139b): global M108 whitener; per-domain candidate pool (n_cap 20000, seed [11, domain]); dictionary = candidates in the [11,100] seeded-permutation order, first 512 atoms; triangle encode on GPU with the registered throttle; closed-form ridge lambda=1.0.
